Interfaces

ConnectRelayOptions

Properties

approvals?
optional approvals?: RelayApprovalChannel;

Where the person decides an act that needs approval: page (the indicator's Approve and Deny, or your own UI), agent (the relay asks through the calling agent's MCP client, and tells this tab the answer), or both (whichever answers first). Default page when attended, agent when unattended. Only with agent or both does the tab accept a decision from the relay.

approvalTtlMs?
optional approvalTtlMs?: number;

How long an approval request stays open, in ms. Default 300000 (five minutes).

backoff?
optional backoff?: object;

Reconnect backoff. Default: from 500 ms, doubling, at most 30000 ms, with jitter.

initialMs?
optional initialMs?: number;
maxMs?
optional maxMs?: number;

describe?
optional describe?: () => object;

What the agent's tab list shows for this page. Default: document.title and location.pathname (never the query).

Returns

object

path
path: string;
title
title: string;

getToken?
optional getToken?: () => string | Promise<string>;

Returns a fresh relay token; called on every connection and before the current one expires, so the connection outlives any one token. Prefer it to token.

Returns

string | Promise<string>

indicator?
optional indicator?: boolean | Element;

The in-page indicator: true (the default when attended) renders a small fixed panel in the page's corner, an Element renders it inside that element, and false (the default when unattended) renders nothing, in which case your own UI must show onStatus and offer stop(), approve(), and deny() when a person is looking.

mode?
optional mode?: RelayMode;

attended (the default): a person is looking at this tab. unattended: the tab runs in a hidden browser session a host started for the person (injectedRelay() says so), so the indicator is off by default and approvals go to the agent's MCP client.

onStatus?
optional onStatus?: (status) => void;

Told after every change of RelayStatus.

requireApproval?
optional requireApproval?: (row) => boolean;

Which acts wait for the person's approval in the page. Default: an action whose effect is risk: "high" or declares confirm. Return false to let an entry run without approval.

disconnect()

Dispose this page connection without revoking access; a later connection may reattach.

Returns

rekey()
rekey(token?): void;

The signed-in person or the tenant changed in the page (a tenant switch without a reload): leave the relay under the old identity, dropping every pending approval, and connect again with token or a fresh getToken(). The relay forgets the old tab record and revokes its token, so no agent of the old principal or tenant reaches the page afterwards.

Type Aliases

RelayApprovalChannel

type RelayApprovalChannel = "page" | "agent" | "both";

Where the person decides an act that needs approval: page, the tab's own agent panel; agent, the calling agent's MCP client (elicitation), with the relay's approval page for sensitive acts; both, whichever answers first.

RelayMode

type RelayMode = "attended" | "unattended";

attended: a person is looking at the tab (the default). unattended: the tab runs in a hidden browser session a host started for the person (@summationai/axe-host), and no one is looking at it.

RelayState

type RelayState = 
  | "connecting"
  | "pairing"
  | "connected"
  | "acting"
  | "reconnecting"
  | "disconnected"
  | "stopped"
  | "refused";

Where the connection stands. connecting: opening the first connection. pairing: connected in development mode and waiting for an agent to pair with the code shown. connected: an agent may act. acting: an agent has read or acted through this tab. reconnecting: the connection dropped and the client is retrying. disconnected: the application disposed this connection without revoking the tab (for example, a component unmounted). stopped: the person pressed Stop (or stop() was called). refused: the relay refused the page (origin, tenant, or token), and the client does not retry.

Functions

connectRelay()

function connectRelay(surface, options): RelayConnection;

Connect this page's surface to a relay so an authorized agent can observe and act on it. Returns at once; the connection opens, authenticates, and reconnects in the background.

Parameters

surface

Surface

options

ConnectRelayOptions

Returns

RelayConnection

devToken()

function devToken(relayUrl): () => Promise<string>;

A getToken for local development: asks the local MCP service (or the lower-level axe relay --dev process) for a development token. The relay serves it on loopback only, to allowed origins only; never use this in production, where an authenticated service issues a token for the signed-in person.

Parameters

relayUrl

string

Returns

() => Promise<string>

injectedRelay()

function injectedRelay(): ConnectRelayOptions | null;

A scoped provider connection as connectRelay options: either window.__AXE_RELAY__ from an optional host, or a one-time browser handoff persisted in this tab's session storage. Reads at call time, never at import. Neither path uses pairing.

Returns

ConnectRelayOptions | null

localMcpService()

function localMcpService(serviceUrl?): ConnectRelayOptions;

Connection options for the local Agent Experience MCP service. The website receives a short-lived development tab token from the service; desktop agents authenticate separately at its /mcp endpoint and pair with the code shown in the page.

Parameters

serviceUrl?

string = LOCAL_MCP_SERVICE_URL

Returns

ConnectRelayOptions

relayOptions()

function relayOptions(fallback): ConnectRelayOptions;

injectedRelay() when a host injected a connection, else fallback (your attended relay, such as the development one). The injected connection replaces the fallback's url, token, mode, approvals, and indicator; the fallback's other options (onStatus, requireApproval, describe, ...) are kept. connectRelay(surface, relayOptions(dev)).

Parameters

fallback

ConnectRelayOptions
